intended_object: The source term a²Φ² of the radial pressure equation ∂_Y P = a(η)²Φ(Y,η)², written as an element of the library's weighted coefficient space `AxisSpace I ε`. The pressure is then recovered as its Y-primitive from the axis. This comes from the docstring, the neighbouring `pressureCoefficient`, and the theorems `pressure_equation`/`pressure_integral`.
explanation:
The body is `product (product a a) (product Φ Φ)`, which is (a·a)·(Φ·Φ) = a²Φ² in the coefficient algebra. `AxisEvaluationAlgebra.profile_product` says this product becomes the pointwise product of profiles on the strip. The library then proves `pressure_equation`: the Y-derivative of the profile of `pressureCoefficient = primitive (pressureSource a Φ)` equals inputValue(a)²·profile(Φ)². It also proves `pressure_integral`: the pressure equals ∫₀^Y a²Φ² dy. These are exactly the `pressure_equation` and `pressure_integral` fields required in `IsScaledSolution`. So the definition is the intended source term.

It is one specific term of a particular PDE reduction (the Navier–Stokes axis ansatz) in the library's own coefficient space. Mathlib has no general version of it, and there is no wider setting it should be stated in. One could also see it as an internal building block of this construction, but it is a concrete named term of the equations, and it is defined correctly.
